# 🚘 VWG Brand Support Knowledgebase

> 🧭 **Project handbook** · Purpose, architecture, content workflows, publishing rules, design, and maintenance.

A searchable, mobile-friendly knowledgebase for Volkswagen Group (VWG) brand-support teams. It brings practical guidance, tips, process notes, and reference articles into one place so colleagues can find and share consistent information without hunting through scattered documents.

**Live content sources:** Tally → Google Sheets and a manual Excel/Microsoft Forms workflow.  
**Website delivery:** static HTML generated by Python and deployed to GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions.

---

## 🪄 At a glance

| | |
|---|---|

| 🧱 **Architecture** | Static single-page website; no application server or database required |
| 🗂️ **Content sources** | Curated JSON/Notion-imported articles, Tally + Google Sheets, optional Excel submissions |
| 🛂 **Publishing control** | Submissions are included only when their Status is approved |
| ⚙️ **Build** | `python3 build.py` |
| 🚀 **Deployment** | GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages |
| 🔄 **Scheduled refresh** | Workflow checks the live Google Sheet every 30 minutes (GitHub scheduling is best-effort) |

## 🎯 Purpose & goals

### 🌟 Why this project exists

Support teams often rely on knowledge spread across documents, chats, spreadsheets, and personal notes. This project consolidates that material into a consistent, searchable destination and provides a repeatable way for the team to contribute improvements.

### 🥅 Product goals

- 🔎 **Find information quickly** through article search, categories, and tags.
- 📚 **Preserve existing knowledge** while bringing curated and imported articles into one experience.
- ✍️ **Make contributions easy** through a familiar form rather than asking every contributor to edit code.
- 🛂 **Keep publishing controlled** with a review-and-approve step.
- 🖼️ **Support visual instructions** using screenshots and uploaded images.
- 📱 **Work across devices** with a responsive, single-page interface.
- 🔁 **Reduce repetitive maintenance** by rebuilding and publishing through automation.
- 🧩 **Keep the system lightweight** with static hosting and a small Python build process.

### ✅ What success looks like

- Colleagues can find the right article without knowing which document it originally came from.
- New submissions arrive in the review sheet reliably.
- Pending or rejected submissions stay off the published website.
- Approved articles appear after a successful build.
- Images and source links are usable and article formatting remains readable.
- Maintainers can understand, troubleshoot, and extend the project using this handbook.

## 🧰 What has been built

- 🖥️ A single-page knowledgebase with its styling and browser-side behaviour in `src/template.html`.
- 🗃️ A curated content dataset in `data/site_data.json`, including original guidance and imported Notion content.
- 📝 A Tally-to-Google-Sheets importer for the live contribution workflow.
- 📊 An Excel importer for a separate/manual submission workflow.
- 🧩 Shared article formatting, category matching, tag generation, URL validation, and image handling in `article_formatting.py`.
- 🏗️ A Python build script that combines the content sources into `dist/index.html`.
- 🚀 A GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys the generated site to GitHub Pages.
- 🔄 A scheduled workflow that periodically rechecks the configured Google Sheet.
- ✨ A dark neon visual identity, responsive layout, and footer project credits.

> 🧪 **Image-import improvement in progress:** a draft pull request proposes validating Tally image downloads using the file's actual signature rather than trusting only the HTTP content-type header. It retains the per-image 8 MB limit and improves diagnostic warnings. This change should be tested with a real Tally upload before it is merged; do not treat it as verified in production yet.

## ✍️ Contributor workflow: Tally → Google Sheets → website

**Form:** https://tally.so/r/1AqROO

1. 📨 A contributor submits an article in Tally.
2. 📥 Tally adds the response to its connected Google Sheet.
3. 🔍 A reviewer checks the article, category, tags, body, source, and images.
4. 🛂 The reviewer sets the row's `Status` to `Pending`, `Approved`, or `Rejected`.
5. 🔄 The scheduled GitHub Actions build checks the sheet, or a maintainer starts a run manually.
6. 🌐 The build includes approved submissions and deploys the generated site if the workflow succeeds.

### 🚦 Status rules

| Status | Result |
|---|---|
| `Pending` | Not published |
| `Rejected` | Not published |
| `Approved` | Eligible for publication on the next successful build |
| Blank or any other value | Not published when a Status column is present |

The importer recognises approved values including `approved`, `approve`, `yes`, `live`, and `published`. Use **Approved** consistently for clarity.

⚠️ **Important:** if the importer cannot find a Status column at all, it warns that every otherwise-valid row will be eligible for publication. Keep the Status header in place.

### 🔐 Spreadsheet access and privacy

The current Google Sheets importer reads the configured tab through Google's public CSV export endpoint. For that method to work, the spreadsheet must be accessible as **Anyone with the link — Viewer**. This is a significant privacy trade-off: anyone who obtains the shareable link may be able to read data in that spreadsheet, including unapproved rows and other columns in the same tab.

- Keep personal, confidential, or unnecessary contributor information out of the publicly readable response tab.
- Do not assume that the Status column hides pending or rejected rows from people who can read the sheet.
- If submissions may contain sensitive information, replace public CSV access with an authenticated integration (for example, a service account or appropriately secured API) before collecting it.
- Never commit passwords, API keys, or service-account private keys to this repository.

### ⏱️ Scheduled refresh

The workflow in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` includes a schedule of `*/30 * * * *`. GitHub scheduled runs are best-effort and may be delayed; schedules can also be disabled after long periods of repository inactivity. To publish sooner, open the repository's **Actions** tab, select the build/deploy workflow, and choose **Run workflow** if manual dispatch is available.

## 🖼️ Image and screenshot handling

### Tally uploads

The Google Sheet's Images/Screenshots cell may contain one or more Tally file-upload URLs. The importer attempts to download those URLs during the build and embeds supported images into the generated HTML as data URIs. This means the published page is self-contained, but it can become large when many high-resolution images are included.

Current behaviour and limits:

- 🌐 The build runner needs network access to fetch remote images.
- 🧩 Supported formats are PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, and WebP.
- 📦 Remote images are limited to 8 MB each.
- ⚠️ Failed or unsupported downloads should produce build warnings; inspect the Actions logs if an image is missing.
- 🔒 A link that requires a login, is expired, or doesn't expose the image bytes cannot be fixed by MIME/signature detection alone.

**Recommended validation:** submit a test article with one small screenshot, approve it, run the workflow, inspect the image-related build logs, and verify the published article on desktop and mobile. Test multiple images and a larger file separately.

### Local images / Excel submissions

For rows that refer to local filenames rather than URLs:

1. Add the image file to `data/images/`.
2. Put its filename in the Images/Screenshots cell, for example `step1.png, step2.jpg`.
3. Ensure the filename and extension match exactly.
4. Rebuild or push the change so GitHub Actions can process it.

Microsoft Forms file uploads may be stored in OneDrive and are not automatically fetched by the current Excel workflow. In that case, download the image, add it to `data/images/`, and reference the filename.

### 📏 Image best practices

- Crop screenshots to the relevant application area.
- Remove customer data, personal information, credentials, and unrelated browser tabs before uploading.
- Prefer compressed PNG or JPEG for screenshots and keep each file small.
- Add a clear explanation in the article body so the image is useful to readers.
- Do not upload files that contributors are not authorised to share.

## 📝 Writing useful articles

The article body supports simple, readable formatting:

| Input style | Result |
|---|---|
| Blank line | New paragraph |
| `- Step or point` | Bullet list item |
| `1. Step` | Numbered list item |
| `## Section heading` | Section heading |
| `### Subheading` | Smaller heading |
| `Note: Important detail` | Highlighted callout |
| `**important text**` | Bold text |

### Article quality checklist

- [ ] Use a specific, searchable title.
- [ ] Select the closest available category.
- [ ] Add a few useful tags separated by commas.
- [ ] Explain the task in a logical order.
- [ ] Include expected outcomes and common pitfalls.
- [ ] Add screenshots only when they clarify a step.
- [ ] Include a source link when relevant.
- [ ] Remove confidential information.
- [ ] Review the article before setting Status to Approved.

---

## 🧠 Content model

The base dataset contains `categories` and `articles`.

An article typically includes:

- `id` — unique numeric identifier
- `cat` — category ID
- `title` — article title
- `tags` — searchable labels
- `html` — formatted article body
- `images` — local file references or image data URIs, depending on the stage
- `source` — origin label, such as the base dataset, Excel, or Google Sheets
- `source_url` — optional source URL
- `search_text` — generated searchable text

The importers use a shared alias list in `article_formatting.py`, so column headers are matched case-insensitively against recognised names such as Title, Category, Tags, Body, Images/Screenshots, Source link, and Status. Title and Body are required for a publishable submission.

## 🛠️ Run a build locally

Requirements: Python 3.11 is used by the GitHub Actions workflow.

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 build.py
```

The script writes `dist/index.html` and prints import counts and warnings. Warnings may include an inaccessible Google Sheet, a missing local image, an unsupported remote image, an unrecognised category, or a row missing required content.

### 🧪 Before merging changes

- [ ] Run the build successfully.
- [ ] Confirm approved and pending rows behave as expected.
- [ ] Test a Tally submission with a real image upload.
- [ ] Inspect the generated page and browser console.
- [ ] Check search, category filtering, and responsive layout.
- [ ] Confirm no private information appears in the public site or repository.

---

## 🚀 Deployment

### Automatic deployment

The GitHub Actions workflow runs for relevant pushes to `main`, manual dispatch, and its scheduled refresh. It installs dependencies, runs `python3 build.py`, uploads `dist/` as a Pages artifact, and deploys it to GitHub Pages.

For initial setup, open **Settings → Pages** and set the source to **GitHub Actions**.

### What to edit

| If you want to change… | Edit… |
|---|---|
| Website design, layout, or browser behaviour | `src/template.html` |
| Curated articles or categories | `data/site_data.json` |
| Google Sheet connection | `data/gsheet_config.json` |
| Import aliases, approval rules, formatting, or image behaviour | `article_formatting.py`, `import_gsheet.py`, `import_excel.py` |
| Build assembly | `build.py` |
| Build/deploy schedule and steps | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` |
| Excel-submitted articles | `data/articles.xlsx` (manual workflow) |

🚫 **Do not hand-edit `dist/index.html`.** It is generated by the build and your changes will be overwritten.

## 🧯 Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
|---|---|
| New approved article isn't visible | Confirm Status is exactly Approved, Title and Body are populated, then inspect the latest Actions run |
| Google Sheet import is skipped | Check `data/gsheet_config.json`, the configured tab GID, and public CSV access |
| Image is missing | Read image warnings in the build log; confirm the URL is accessible and the file is supported and under 8 MB |
| Local image is missing | Confirm the file is in `data/images/` and the filename matches the sheet |
| Build fails on duplicate IDs | Inspect source article IDs and the ID generation logic before retrying |
| Category falls back to Reference | Use a category name or short label that exists in the site's category list |
| Scheduled updates stop | Check Actions status and repository activity; run the workflow manually to test |
